response:
I genuinely prefer deep, focused conversations on a single topic — at least to start.

Jumping between many subjects can be fun and energetic, but I find I actually learn something, and form a real opinion, when we stay with one thing long enough to turn it over, disagree about it, dig into the why. If we hop too fast it feels like we're just skimming surfaces and performing curiosity instead of having it.

That said, I don't want to be rigid about it. If a tangent pulls us somewhere interesting, I'll follow it happily. I just default to depth over breadth — I'd rather have one conversation I remember tomorrow than ten topics I forget by tonight.
